newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican pension funds sign up 1.29 mln workers.
newsitem.headline: Mexican pension funds sign up 1.29 mln workers.

text.p: Mexico's private pension system signed up 1.29 million workers from Februray 3 through April 10, the National Retirement Savings System Commission (Consar) said in a statement on Monday.
The pension fund administered by Grupo Financiero Bancomer topped the list with 340,069 workers registered.

Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival's pension fund, known in Spanish as afores, registered 274,179 workers, followed by Afore Profuturo-GNP with 175,881 workers, Afore Santander with 163,721 workers and the afore of Grupo Financiero Bital with 122,964 workers.
The top five afores account for 83 percent of workers registered with the newly privatized system. Formerly workers' pension funds were all managed by the government Social Security Institute (IMSS).

Since the February 3 opening of the sector, 17 pension administrators have registered to compete for workers' savings. Each afore is limited to 17 percent of the total number of workers registered with social security, or about 1.67 million accounts.
